name: Baby Green
lede: Baby Green is a vivid, pale yellow-green listed across the CSS, RAL and ISCC-NBS systems, and far more saturated on screen than most of what it matches in old paint.

sections.title: A name in the library
sections.body:
This bright green appears across several standard lists: the CSS color keywords, the German RAL system (close to RAL 6029 and RAL 6021), the ISCC-NBS dictionary of 1955, and the xkcd color survey [1]. No single source dates its first use; it reads as a modern, screen-native green rather than a dye or pigment name [1]. The nearest color-graph neighbor is [[light-green]], 3.8 units away, with [[seafoam]], [[easter-green]] and [[light-pastel-green]] all close behind [2].

Munsell gives 1.3G 9.1/10.5, very light and strongly saturated, a combination rare in historical pigments [1]. The hex #8CFF9E sits near the edge of what a screen can display; almost nothing painted before photography reaches this brightness [1].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: At a looser match (ΔE 15), our archive finds only 3 of 23,781 paintings, as photographed, and the strongest is a well-known case: Vincent van Gogh's *Roses* (1890), at the National Gallery of Art [3]. The pink pigment in that painting has faded over more than a century, and much of what was once rose-pink now reads, in photographs, as this pale green [3]. His *Still Life of Oranges and Lemons with Blue Gloves* (1889) is a weaker second match [3]. The rarity of this exact green elsewhere in the archive reflects how recent and screen-bound the color itself is, not its absence in nature [3].

questions.q: Why does Van Gogh's *Roses* (1890) now match a bright screen green?
choices: Its pink pigment has faded over time, as photographed today
Van Gogh originally painted it green
It is a different painting entirely
questions.answer: Its pink pigment has faded over time, as photographed today

questions.q: True or false: most pre-photography pigments can reach the brightness of Baby Green.

openers: Our best archive match for this bright green is a Van Gogh painting that was originally pink.
